Subject: MedData: schedule deep technical review & on-call prep

Alex — quick intro and ask. Thanks again for the productive discovery last week. MedData asked for a focused, multi‑stakeholder technical review that covers: VPC/connectivity options for on‑prem routing, IAM and service account patterns, and an on‑call runbook for incident escalation. We want AE + SE + your infra/security/procurement to be present so the outcome is an actionable roll‑out plan.

Proposed high-level agenda (30–60m):
- 10m: Goals and constraints (MedData)
- 25m: Architecture walk (Redwood SE) — VPC, routing, firewall/peering options, NAT
- 15m: IAM/service account patterns and audit logs
- 10m: Runbook + next steps (procurement/ops inputs)

Current ask: can you share 3 slots next week (PST) where your infra + security + procurement can attend? We can commit AE + SE + a delivery manager. If you prefer a longer workshop (90m) we can include a deeper network config review; say that in your reply and we’ll adjust.

I’ll attach a brief agenda and a runbook template that we can prepopulate.

Attachments: redwood_vpc-oncall-agenda.pdf (application/pdf), redwood_runbook-template.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

—

- Wed 12/15: 10:30–11:30 or 14:00–15:30
- Thu 12/16: 09:00–10:00 or 16:00–17:30

We have two asks before we lock a slot:
1) If you choose the 60–90m option, please confirm which team members from Redwood will stay for the full window (we’ll need both the SE and someone who can speak procurement/contract timelines).
2) Can you circulate a short pre‑read with network prerequisites (e.g., IP ranges, required inbound/outbound ports, any specific VPN config) so our network team can validate ahead of time?

procurement@meddata.com: we may need a short procurement/PO checklist in the agenda if this workshop surfaces changes to data residency or SLA requirements. sec-ops@meddata.com: flag anything else we should bring.

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Alex — great, thanks for the slots. We can cover the full 90m if that’s what you prefer; SE + delivery engineer will join (I’ll be the lead). Quick pre‑read items below so your network/security teams have context:

Pre‑read / checklist (short)
- Public endpoints: none required for private deployments; if you need hosted API fallback, we’ll list IP ranges and egress ports.
- Common ports: 443 outbound (TLS) to Redwood control plane for metrics/health; 22 only if on‑prem support is requested (otherwise we use agentless diagnostics).
- VPN/Peering: support for route‑based VPNs and VPC peering; we’ll present both options and tradeoffs.
- IAM: recommend using short‑lived service accounts via your existing SSO provider; we’ll show sample policies.
- Logging: we’ll propose an audit log forwarding pattern (CloudWatch/Stackdriver/Splunk) — indicate what you use and we’ll tailor.

I’ve attached a concise agenda and a runbook template for you to look at. If you can send the IP ranges and the name of your logging endpoint before EOD tomorrow, we’ll prepopulate a section in the runbook.

Attachment: redwood_vpc-oncall-agenda.pdf (application/pdf)

Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
